newsitem.title: USA: HemaSure seeking $275 million in suit.
newsitem.headline: HemaSure seeking $275 million in suit.

text.p: HemaSure Inc said on Tuesday that it was seeking $275 million in a suit against Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc over the cancelled sale of Pharmacia & Upjohn blood plasma unit.
A spokeswoman for Marlborough, Mass.-based Hemasure said the suit was filed on Friday in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan.
Hemasure is alleging that Pharmacia & Upjohn called off the sale of its Sweden-based plasma unit after 14 months of negotiations with Hemasure, the spokeswoman said.
A Britain-based spokesman for Pharmacia & Upjohn acknowledged that a suit had been filed related to the plasma division but declined to discuss details.
During the negotiations with Pharmacia & Upjohn, Hemasure acquired Novo Nordisk A/S's loss-making plasma business with the plan of merging it with the Pharmacia & Upjohn unit, the spokeswoman said.
HemaSure took on $38 million in "obligations and commitments" with the Novo Nordisk acquisition, she said.
In the suit HemaSure is seeking $175 million in compensatory damages and $100 million in punative damages, the spokeswoman said.
